study: Two-robot shared-exit navigation with and without communication
change_reason: The previous in-arena visual target was difficult to observe and the preceding exclusionary run ended by controller time limits without a task-monitor verdict. This additive hammer-shaped world provides a real wall opening, a green passage and a wider external reception area. It also keeps the two post-exit holding regions physically separated.
world_file_note: New additive world. Earlier worlds and all bags remain unchanged. The opening and reception area are physical geometry. Coloured parking guides are horizontal zero-thickness visual surfaces without boundingObject; no raised marker is present.
robot_radius_m_source: e-puck2 nominal 70 mm body diameter plus a small geometric margin

exit.interpretation: Crossing the real east-wall opening and entering the green neck. This is the shared information target, not the final completion region.

parking_zones.note: After entering the green neck, each robot receives its own holding target in the wider reception area. The task monitor requires both robots to remain inside their assigned regions continuously for goal_hold_time_s.

robot_a.role: informed: navigates directly to the known opening

robot_b.role: uninformed: follows the preregistered search route until the opening is known

max_runtime_s_note: Expanded observation ceiling for the longer real-exit route. Reaching this ceiling is a task failure, never successful completion.
nominal_speed_mps_note: Unchanged from the preceding exclusionary configuration and identical in communication-off/on conditions.

on.robot_a_navigation: same direct route plus bounded GoalAnnouncement publication
on.robot_b_navigation: same search until receipt of a valid GoalAnnouncement, then direct to the opening
